extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or beginning graduate students studying algebraic topology
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook chapter presenting definitions, fundamental theorems, constructions, and computations in singular homology (reduced and relative homology, homotopy invariance, exact sequences, excision, barycentric subdivision) with proofs and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition over path components (Proposition 2.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corresponding to the decomposition of a space X into its path-components X_α there is an isomorphism H_n(X) ≈ ⊕_α H_n(X_α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: singular simplices have path-connected image so C_n(X) splits as direct sum of C_n(X_α); boundary maps preserve decomposition so Ker ∂ and Im ∂ split similarly, hence homology splits. Use whenever X decomposes into path components to reduce computations to components.

rubrics_metrics.name: H_0 for path-connected spaces (Proposition 2.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is nonempty and path-connected then H_0(X) ≈ Z; more generally H_0(X) is a direct sum of Z's, one for each path-component of X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct augmentation ε : C_0(X) → Z by ε(∑ n_i σ_i) = ∑ n_i; for path-connected X, Ker ε = Im ∂_1 so ε induces isomorphism H_0(X) ≈ Z. Use ε and paths to exhibit boundaries showing cycles with total coefficient zero are boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homology of a point (Proposition 2.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a point then H_n(X) = 0 for n > 0 and H_0(X) ≈ Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a unique singular n-simplex for each n; the chain complex alternates isomorphisms and zero maps so homology is trivial except H_0 ≈ Z. Use as base case for inductive computations and reduced homology normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced homology and augmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced homology is defined by augmenting the singular chain complex C_* (X) with ε : C_0(X) → Z (ε(∑ n_i σ_i) = ∑ n_i) and taking homology of the augmented complex; for nonempty X this makes a point have trivial homology in all dimensions including 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relation to ordinary homology: ~H_n(X) = H_n(X) for n > 0 and H_0(X) ≈ ~H_0(X) ⊕ Z. Require X nonempty to avoid homology in dimension -1. Think of the extra Z as generated by the empty simplex [∅].

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain maps induce homomorphisms on homology (Proposition 2.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: A chain map between chain complexes induces homomorphisms between the homology groups of the two complexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If f_♯ : C_n(X) → C_n(Y) satisfies f_♯ ∂ = ∂ f_♯ then f_♯ takes cycles to cycles and boundaries to boundaries, hence induces f_* : H_n(X) → H_n(Y). This formal algebraic statement underlies induced maps of topological maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality and identities for induced maps
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) (f ◦ g)_* = f_* g_* for compositions; (ii) id_* = id.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These trivial but important properties follow from composition properties of chain maps and ensure homology is a functor from topological spaces to graded abelian groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy invariance of induced maps (Theorem 2.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two maps f,g : X → Y are homotopic, they induce the same homomorphism f_* = g_* : H_n(X) → H_n(Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct prism operators P : C_n(X) → C_{n+1}(Y) from a homotopy F so that ∂P = g_♯ − f_♯ − P ∂. Then for a cycle α, g_♯(α) − f_♯(α) = ∂P(α), hence they represent the same homology class. Use prism operator argument to prove chain homotopy between f_♯ and g_♯.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain-homotopic chain maps give same map on homology (Proposition 2.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two chain maps are chain-homotopic, they induce the same homomorphism on homology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete relation: a chain homotopy P satisfying ∂P + P∂ = g_♯ − f_♯ shows g_♯ and f_♯ induce identical maps on homology. This is the algebraic formulation of homotopy invariance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy equivalence induces isomorphisms (Corollary 2.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f : X → Y is a homotopy equivalence then f_* : H_n(X) → H_n(Y) is an isomorphism for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from homotopy invariance and functoriality: inverse up to homotopy yields inverse maps on homology. Use to compute homology of contractible spaces: H_n = 0 for all n (reduced viewpoint).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of exact sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence ... → A_{n+1} →^{α_{n+1}} A_n →^{α_n} A_{n-1} → ... is exact if Ker α_n = Im α_{n+1} for each n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to chain complex plus trivial homology; use short exact sequences (0→A→B→C→0) to encode injections, surjections, and quotient identifications. Many topological relationships are expressed via exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence for pair when A is deformation retract of neighborhood (Theorem 2.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a space and A ⊂ X is a nonempty closed subspace that is a deformation retract of some neighborhood in X, there is a long exact sequence ... → H_n(A) →^{i_*} H_n(X) →^{j_*} H_n(X/A) →^{∂} H_{n-1}(A) → ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here i is inclusion A ↪ X and j is quotient X → X/A. The boundary map ∂ is constructed algebraically; an element of H_n(X/A) can be represented by a chain α in X whose boundary lies in A, and ∂[α] is the homology class of ∂α in H_{n-1}(A). Pairs satisfying the hypothesis are called 'good pairs' (e.g., CW complexes with subcomplex).

rubrics_metrics.name: Good pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Pairs (X,A) where A is nonempty closed and is a deformation retract of some neighborhood in X are called good pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good pairs guarantee hypotheses needed for Theorem 2.13 and allow relative homology to be compared with homology of quotient X/A. Typical example: (CW complex, subcomplex).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of homology of spheres via long exact sequence (Corollary 2.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: H_i(S^n) ≈ Z for i = n and H_i(S^n) = 0 for i ≠ n (reduced groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: use pair (D^n, S^{n-1}) with D^n contractible so many terms vanish and induction on n starting from S^0. Use the long exact sequence of the pair to deduce isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonexistence of retraction and Brouwer fixed point (Corollary 2.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: ∂D^n is not a retract of D^n; hence every map f : D^n → D^n has a fixed point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homology argument: a retraction r would make composition r_* ∘ i_* the identity on H_{n-1}(∂D^n) ≈ Z, but one of these maps is zero, contradiction. Use homological obstruction to retractions and fixed points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of relative homology H_n(X,A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative homology is defined as the homology of the quotient chain complex C_n(X,A) = C_n(X)/C_n(A) with induced boundary; elements are represented by relative cycles α ∈ C_n(X) with ∂α ∈ C_{n-1}(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A relative cycle α is trivial in H_n(X,A) iff α = ∂β + γ with β ∈ C_{n+1}(X) and γ ∈ C_n(A). Intuitively H_n(X,A) is 'homology of X modulo A'. While C_n(X)/C_n(A) can be seen as subgroup of C_n(X) generated by simplices not contained in A, boundaries may not preserve that subgroup, so the quotient viewpoint is preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence of a short exact sequence of chain complexes (algebraic machinery)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short exact sequence of chain complexes 0→A→B→C→0 yields a long exact sequence in homology ... → H_n(A) → H_n(B) → H_n(C) →^{∂} H_{n-1}(A) → ...; the boundary map ∂ is constructed algebraically by lifting cycles and taking boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction details: for a cycle c ∈ C_n with c = j(b), take ∂b ∈ Ker j = Im i so ∂b = i(a) and define ∂[c] = [a]. Well-definedness is checked by uniqueness and independence of choices. This algebraic theorem underlies the topological long exact sequences for pairs/triples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness properties in the long exact sequence (Theorem 2.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the long exact sequence obtained from a short exact sequence of chain complexes: Im i_* = Ker j_*, Im j_* = Ker ∂, Im ∂ = Ker i_*, and the six exactness verifications described algebraically (diagram chasing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof proceeds by checking the six inclusions via lifts and boundaries; key technique is diagram chasing. Use these identities to translate between kernel/image relations and quotient identifications in homology computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative-to-absolute relation and reduced long exact sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an analogous long exact sequence of reduced homology groups for a pair (X,A) with A ≠ ∅; in particular H_n(X,A) equals the corresponding reduced absolute homology for A ≠ ∅.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the augmented chain complexes and the short exact sequence augmented in dimension -1 to pass from relative to reduced absolute homology. This identification is useful in many computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key examples: H_i(D^n, ∂D^n) and H_n(X,x_0)
rubrics_metrics.description: H_i(D^n, ∂D^n) ≈ Z for i = n and 0 otherwise; for a pair (X,x_0) with basepoint x_0, H_n(X,x_0) ≈ ~H_n(X) for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples follow from applying the long exact sequence of a pair and using contractibility of D^n or triviality of H_n(point). They serve as standard computations and checks for relative homology formalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induced maps and homotopy invariance for relative homology (Proposition 2.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: A map of pairs f : (X,A) → (Y,B) (with f(A) ⊂ B) induces f_♯ : C_n(X,A) → C_n(Y,B) and hence f_* : H_n(X,A) → H_n(Y,B); if f and g are homotopic through maps of pairs then f_* = g_* on relative homology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The relative prism operator is obtained by passing the absolute prism operator to quotients since it takes C_n(A) into C_{n+1}(B); chain-homotopy arguments as in the absolute case apply verbatim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence of a triple
rubrics_metrics.description: For a triple B ⊂ A ⊂ X there is a long exact sequence ... → H_n(A,B) → H_n(X,B) → H_n(X,A) → H_{n-1}(A,B) → ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This arises from the short exact sequences 0 → C_n(A,B) → C_n(X,B) → C_n(X,A) → 0; use triple sequences to relate various relative homology groups and reduce computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excision Theorem (Theorem 2.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Z ⊂ A ⊂ X with closure(Z) contained in interior(A), the inclusion (X−Z, A−Z) ↪ (X,A) induces isomorphisms H_n(X−Z, A−Z) → H_n(X,A) for all n. Equivalently, if A and B have interiors covering X then inclusion (B, A∩B) ↪ (X,A) induces H_n(B, A∩B) → H_n(X,A) isomorphisms for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate between formulations by setting B = X−Z. Excision is proven using barycentric subdivision to produce small simplices subordinate to covers; it's central to local-to-global arguments in homology and to computing relative homology by replacing pairs with more convenient ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdivision and small-chain techniques (Proposition 2.21 and construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an open cover U of X, define C_n^U(X) as subgroup of chains whose simplices lie in some element of the cover. The inclusion i : C_n^U(X) ↪ C_n(X) is a chain-homotopy equivalence: there is a chain map ρ : C_n(X) → C_n^U(X) with ιρ and ρι chain-homotopic to identities, hence H_n^U(X) ≈ H_n(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via barycentric subdivision: define linear subdivision operator S on linear chains, construct chain homotopy T with ∂T + T∂ = id − S, extend to singular chains via pushforward by simplices, iterate subdivisions to make simplex diameters arbitrarily small (diameter decreases by factor n/(n+1) per subdivision) and then build ρ = id − ∂D − D∂ with D summing T S^i. This operator ρ lands in chains subordinate to the cover and yields the homotopy inverse. Use this small-chain technique to implement excision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barycentric subdivision properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Barycentric subdivision of an n-simplex decomposes it into n! (and more generally many) simplices whose vertices are barycenters of faces; the diameter of each simplex in the subdivision is at most n/(n+1) times the diameter of the original simplex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterating subdivision shrinks diameters to 0 as r→∞ since product over iterations tends to 0; crucially the factor n/(n+1) is independent of simplex shape. Use this geometric control to guarantee eventual smallness relative to open covers (Lebesgue number arguments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdivision operator S and chain homotopy to identity
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a subdivision operator S : C_n(X) → C_n(X) (built from barycentric subdivision) which is a chain map (∂S = S∂) and a chain homotopy T with ∂T + T∂ = id − S; iterates S^m are chain-homotopic to the identity via D_m = ∑_{i=0}^{m-1} T S^i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This algebraic relation is used to construct D and then ρ = id − ∂D − D∂ producing the map into small-chain subcomplex. Keep track that S is identity on 0-simplices and augmented -1 level for uniform treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient-to-absolute isomorphism for good pairs (Proposition 2.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: For good pairs (X,A) the quotient map q : (X,A) → (X/A, A/A) induces isomorphisms q_* : H_n(X,A) → H_n(X/A) for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a neighborhood V deformation retracting to A and a commutative diagram comparing triples and quotients; excision and deformation retraction arguments show the relevant maps are isomorphisms. This identifies relative homology with homology of the quotient for good pairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative homology as reduced absolute homology for good pairs (final observation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For good pairs (X,A), relative homology H_n(X,A) can be expressed as reduced absolute homology of the quotient X/A (i.e., H_n(X,A) ≅ ~H_n(X/A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from Proposition 2.22 and the identification of A/A as the basepoint in the quotient; it provides a standard technique to move between relative computations and reduced absolute homology computations. For arbitrary pairs one can adjoin cones to achieve similar identifications.
